repos.readme_excerpt:
# Hermes Agent ☤

Hermes Agent | Hermes Desktop

**The self-improving AI agent built by [Nous Research](https://nousresearch.com).** It's the only agent with a built-in learning loop — it creates skills from experience, improves them during use, nudges itself to persist knowledge, searches its own past conversations, and builds a deepening model of who you are across sessions. Run it on a $5 VPS, a GPU cluster, or serverless infrastructure that costs nearly nothing when idle. It's not tied to your laptop — talk to it from Telegram while it works on a cloud VM. Use any model you want — [Nous Portal](https://portal.nousresearch.com), OpenRouter, OpenAI, your own endpoint, and [many others](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/integrations/providers). Switch with `hermes model` — no code changes, no lock-in.
A real terminal interfaceFull TUI with multiline editing, slash-command autocomplete, conversation history, interrupt-and-redirect, and streaming tool output.
Lives where you doTelegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, and CLI — all from a single gateway process. Voice memo transcription, cross-platform conversation continuity.
A closed learning loopAgent-curated memory with periodic nudges. Autonomous skill creation after complex tasks. Skills self-improve during use. FTS5 session search with LLM summarization for cross-session recall. Honcho dialectic user modeling. Compatible with the agentskills.io open standard.
Scheduled automationsBuilt-in cron scheduler with delivery to any platform. Daily reports, nightly backups, weekly audits — all in natural language, running unattended.
Delegates and parallelizesSpawn isolated subagents for parallel workstreams. Write Python scripts that call tools via RPC, collapsing multi-step pipelines into zero-context-cost turns.
Runs anywhere, not just your laptopSeven terminal backends — local, Docker, SSH, Singularity, Modal, Daytona, and Vercel Sandbox. Daytona and Modal offer serverless persistence — your agent's environment hibernates when idle and wakes on demand, costing nearly nothing between sessions. Run it on a $5 VPS or a GPU cluster.
Research-readyBatch trajectory generation, trajectory compression for training the next generation of tool-calling models.
--- ## Quick Install ### Linux, macOS, WSL2 ```bash curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash ``` ### Windows (native, PowerShell) > **Heads up:** Native Windows runs Hermes without WSL — CLI, gateway, TUI, and tools all work natively. If you'd rather use WSL2, the Linux/macOS one-liner above works there too. Found a bug? Please [file issues](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues). Run this in PowerShell: ```powershell iex (irm https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.ps1) ``` The source installer delegates Python 3.14, Node.js, npm, ripgrep, FFmpeg, and Python dependencies to PM. If Git is absent, it stages the verified Git for Windows archive in Hermes' tool store. It does not replace your system Git. See [installation methods](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/getting-started/installation) for the separate MSIX/App Installer package and its update ownership. > **Android / Termux:** A signed APT repository is available for aarch64 devices, with a `stable` channel (tagged releases) and a prerelease `canary` channel. The package includes Python, Node.js, and the TUI. Use the [Termux guide](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/getting-started/termux), not the desktop/server installer script. > > **Windows:** Native Windows is fully supported — the PowerShell one-liner above installs everything. If you'd rather use WSL2, the Linux command works there too. Native Windows install lives under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`; WSL2 installs under `~/.hermes` as on Linux. After installation: ```bash source ~/.bashrc # reload shell (or: source ~/.zshrc) hermes # start chatting! ``` ### Troubleshooting #### Windows Defender or antivirus flags `uv.exe` as malware If your antivirus (Bitdefender, Windows Defender, etc.) quarantines `uv.exe` from the Hermes `bin` folder (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\bin\uv.exe`), this is a **false positive**. The file is Astral's `uv` — the Rust Python package manager Hermes bundles to manage its Python environment. ML-based antivirus engines commonly flag unsigned Rust binaries that download and install packages. **To verify your copy is authentic:** ```powershell # Install GitHub CLI if needed winget install --id GitHub.cli # Login to GitHub gh auth login # Run verification $uv = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\hermes\bin\uv.exe" $ver = (& $uv --version).Split(' ')[1] [Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12 $zip = "$env:TEMP\uv.zip" Invoke-WebRequest "https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/download/$ver/uv-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip" -OutFile $zip -UseBasicParsing gh attestation verify $zip --repo astral-sh/uv Expand-Archive $zip "$env:TEMP\uv_x" -Force (Get-FileHash "$env:TEMP\uv_x\uv.exe").Hash -eq (Get-FileHash $uv).Hash ``` If attestation says "Verification succeeded" and the last line prints `True`, you're good. **To whitelist Hermes:** - **Windows Defender:** Run PowerShell as Admin → `Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\hermes\bin"` - **Bitdefender:** Add an exception in the Bitdefender console (Protection > Antivirus > Settings > Manage Exceptions) - Whitelist the **folder**, not the file hash — Hermes updates `uv` and the hash changes every version For more context, see the upstream Astral reports: [astral-sh/uv#13553](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/13553), [astral-sh/uv#15011](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/15011), [astral-sh/uv#10079](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/10079). --- ## Getting Started ```bash hermes # Interactive CLI — start a conversation hermes model # Choose your LLM provider and model hermes tools # Configure which tools are enabled hermes config set # Set individual config values hermes config get # Print individual config values hermes gateway # Start the messaging gateway (Telegram, Discord, etc.) hermes setup # Run the full setup wizard (configures everything at once) hermes claw migrate # Migrate from OpenClaw (if coming from OpenClaw) hermes update # Update to the latest version hermes doctor # Diagnose any issues ``` 📖 **[Full documentation →](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/)** --- ## Skip the API-key collection — Nous Portal Hermes works with whatever provider you want — that's not changing. But if you'd rather not collect five separate API keys for the model, web search, image generation, TTS, and a cloud browser, **[Nous Portal](https://portal.nousresearch.com)** covers all of them under one subscription: - **300+ models** — pick any of them with `/model ` - **Tool Gateway** — web search, image generation (FAL), text-to-speech (OpenAI), cloud browser (Browser Use), all routed through your sub. No extra accounts. One command from a fresh install: ```bash hermes setup --portal ``` That logs you in via OAuth, sets Nous as your provider, and turns on the Tool Gateway. Check what's wired up any time with `hermes portal info`. Full details on the [Tool Gateway docs page](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/tool-gateway). You can still bring your own keys per-tool whenever you want — the gateway is per-backend, not all-or-nothing. --- ## CLI vs Messaging Quick Reference Hermes has two entry points: start the terminal UI with `hermes`, or run the gateway and talk to it from Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, or Email. Once you're in a conversation, many slash commands are shared across both interfaces. | Action | CLI | Messaging platforms | | ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Start chatting | `hermes` | Run `hermes gateway setup` + `hermes gateway start`, then send the bot a message | | Start fresh conversation | `/new` or `/reset` | `/new` or `/reset` | | Change model | `/model [provider:model]` | `/model [provider:model]` | | Set a personality | `/personality [name]` | `/personality [name]` | | Retry or undo the last turn | `/retry`, `/undo` | `/retry`, `/undo` | | Compress context / check usage | `/compress`, `/usage`, `/insights [--days N]` | `/compress`, `/usage`, `/insights [days]` | | Browse skills | `/skills` or `/` | `/` | | Interrupt current work | `Ctrl+C` or send a new message | `/stop` or send a new message | | Platform-specific status | `/platforms` | `/status`, `/sethome` | For the full command lists, see the [CLI guide](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/cli) and the [Messaging Gateway guide](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/messaging). --- ## Documentation All documentation lives at **[hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/)**: | Section | What's Covered | | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | | [Quickstart](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/getting-started/quickstart) | Install → setup → first conversation in 2 minutes | | [CLI Usage](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/cli) | Commands, keybindings, personalities, sessions | | [Configuration](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/configuration) | Config file, providers, models, all options | | [Messaging Gateway](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/messaging) | Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, Home Assistant | | [Security](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/security) | Command approval, DM pairing, container isolation | | [Tools & Toolsets](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/tools) | 40+ tools, toolset system, terminal backends | | [Skills System](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/skills) | Procedural memory, Skills Hub, creating skills | | [Memory](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/memory) | Persistent memory, user profiles, best practices | | [MCP Integration](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/mcp) | Connect any MCP server for extended capabilities | | [Cron Scheduling](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/cron) | Scheduled tasks with platform delivery | | [Context Files](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/context-files) | Project context that shapes every conversation | | [Architecture](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/architecture) | Project structure, agent loop, key classes | | [Contributing](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/contributing) | Development setup, PR process, code style | | [CLI Reference](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/reference/cli-commands) | All commands and flags | | [Environment Variables](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/reference/environment-variables) | Complete env var reference | --- ## Migrating from OpenClaw If you're coming from OpenClaw, Hermes can automatically import your settings, memories, skills, and API keys. **During first-time setup:** The setup wizard (`hermes setup`) automatically detects `~/.openclaw` and offers to migrate before configuration begins. **Anytime after install:** ```bash hermes claw migrate # Interactive migration (full preset) hermes claw migrate --dry-run # Preview what would be migrated hermes claw migrate --preset user-data # Migrate without secrets hermes claw migrate --overwrite # Overwrite existing conflicts ``` What gets imported: - **SOUL.md** — persona file - **Memories** — MEMORY.md and USER.md entries - **Skills** — user-created skills → `~/.hermes/skills/openclaw-imports/` - **Command allowlist** — approval patterns - **Messaging settings** — platform configs, allowed users, working directory - **API keys** — allowlisted secrets (Telegram, OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, ElevenLabs) - **TTS assets** — workspace audio files - **Workspace instructions** — AGENTS.md (with `--workspace-target`) See `hermes claw migrate --help` for all options, or use the `openclaw-migration` skill for an interactive agent-guided migration with dry-run previews. --- ## Contributing We welcome contributions! See the [Contributing Guide](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/contributing) for development setup, code style, and PR process. Start with the [PM developer workflow](website/docs/reference/package-management.md#developer-workflow) for activation, daily use, dependency changes, and leaving the environment. [Development Setup](CONTRIBUTING.md#development-setup) covers the separate test environment and verification commands. --- ## Community - 💬 [Discord](https://discord.gg/NousResearch) - 📚 [Skills Hub](https://agentskills.io) - 🐛 [Issues](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues) - 🔌 [computer-use-linux](https://github.com/avifenesh/computer-use-linux) — Linux desktop-control MCP server for Hermes and other MCP hosts, with AT-SPI accessibility trees, Wayland/X11 input, screenshots, and compositor window targeting. - 🔌 [HermesClaw](https://github.com/AaronWong1999/hermesclaw) — Community WeChat bridge: Run Hermes Agent and OpenClaw on the same WeChat account. --- ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Built by [Nous Research](https://nousresearch.com).

repos.name: CCBaga
repos.readme_excerpt:
CCBaga

A native macOS, Linux and Windows toolkit for a cleaner workspace and an environment you can verify.

Claude identities · Browser fingerprints · System settings · Network Skill

Features · Installation · Updates · Quick start · Usage guide · Architecture · Development · Contributing

![CCBaga: native control, observable environments](docs/readme-hero.png) **Intended use:** CCBaga is intended solely for people residing or traveling abroad to manage their own Claude identities. Use that violates Anthropic's official terms of service is prohibited. CCBaga brings local maintenance and environment setup into one focused desktop workflow. Inspect Claude data before removing it, rotate your companion browser's fingerprint and restart it, align system settings with a selected region, and compare real browser readings with the machine and network exit. Two applications work together: **CCBaga-A** owns native operations; **CCBaga-B** runs an isolated Fingerprint Chromium profile. Browser measurements return to the host through a local session. Changing a setting and verifying its effect are separate steps. ## Features
Local Claude identities

Archive the current local identity, switch to a saved identity or start with an empty workspace. Choose what stays shared and what moves with each identity.		 Fingerprint & restart

Generate a fresh seed, apply the selected region's language and timezone, then restart the companion browser.		 Real environment checks

Compare browser and machine readings with the actual network exit. Passing measured checks produces a green page and a large checkmark.
Native system settings

Apply timezone, preferred language and region settings. Open desktop controls for location and permissions; see platform-specific limits.		 AI-guided network setup

Three simple steps, a coding-agent selector and a copyable Skill installation prompt. Give the AI your files and connection details; it handles the commands.		 Claude Code CLI tools

Detect the installation method and version. Uninstall or reinstall through native, npm/bun, Homebrew or WinGet workflows.
**One region selector. Four everyday actions.** Easy setup puts browser cache cleanup, fingerprint rotation, timezone/language reset and identity archiving on the same page. The sidebar keeps advanced controls in Network, Claude identities, Browser and Computer. The interface supports **English and Chinese**, with shared YAML catalogs. Switching the interface language does not change the computer or browser language. The bilingual **Usage guide** covers common actions and data boundaries. See the [full guide](docs/usage.md). ## Installation **Platforms:** macOS 12 or later on Apple Silicon; Linux x86_64 with GTK 3 and WebKitGTK 4.1; Windows 10/11 x86_64. Intel macOS and Linux ARM64 are not supported. Linux x86_64 packages include DEB, RPM, AppImage and Arch/pacman formats, with the companion browser included. See [Linux setup](docs/linux.md) for installation and platform limits. Official versions are published exclusively by the project owner, **liseami**. Windows x86_64 uses one NSIS setup installer containing both A and B. The installer is not Authenticode signed and may show SmartScreen; managed security policy can block it. See [Windows setup](docs/windows.md) for installation, toolchains and platform behaviors. ### macOS Download the official installer from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/liseami/CCBaga/releases/latest). The distribution package is named `CCBaga--macos-arm64.dmg`. It contains both applications: | Application | Installed bundle | Role | | --- | --- | --- | | CCBaga-A | `CCBaga-A.app` | Identity management, system settings and environment verification | | CCBaga-B | `CCBaga-B.app` | Companion browser with a dedicated profile | Download **one DMG**; it contains both applications. There is no separate browser download. The installer uses the same pixel-art style as this README. 1. Open the disk image and drag **both applications** into Applications. 2. Launch CCBaga-A. It starts the companion browser automatically. 3. Choose English at the bottom of the sidebar if needed. Source builds are available through the [development guide](#development). ## Updates Use **Check for updates** at the bottom of CCBaga-A’s sidebar. Startup checks quietly; installation only starts when you choose **Update and restart**. Downloads show actual progress and are verified before installation. Failed downloads can be retried; a failed restart does not download the update again. On **macOS**, in-app updates replace A; use the latest DMG to update both apps. On **Windows**, a verified NSIS update installs both A and B after closing this companion browser. On **Linux**, use the package manager or full package. ## Quick start ### Everyday setup Open **Easy setup**, select a country or region, then choose an action. Browser fingerprint rotation closes and restarts CCBaga-B, so save unfinished browser work first. Selecting a region changes language, timezone and regional settings; it does **not** change your public IP. ### Claude identities Open **Claude identities** to manage the local state of both Claude Code and Claude Desktop. Choose **Empty identity** to archive the current state before leaving a fresh workspace, or choose a saved identity to restore it. Every switch saves the outgoing identity first. Expand **Keep in workspace** to choose retention for skills and commands, plugins, MCP configuration, personal settings, project records, conversation history, and caches/logs. Login data always moves with an archived identity. Project source outside Claude's own data directories is not scanned. A confirmation names the outgoing identity and summarizes what stays in the workspace before closing recognized Claude processes. Portrait identity cards scroll horizontally with spring motion and subtle hover tilt. The white empty identity stays first, followed by the current local account with available name, email and organization information. **Archive** saves the current state and leaves an empty identity. Select a saved card to restore that identity. **Direct delete** removes selected current data without creating an archive; deleting a saved card removes only that archive. Both deletion actions require an explicit confirmation. A local SQLite database tracks names, policies and recovery state. Data is compressed into an authenticated, encrypted `.baga` container outside Claude's working directories. Archive verification precedes workspace changes; failed switches roll back, and an interrupted switch exposes recovery. Recovery also saves the pre-recovery state. Ordinary archive tools cannot open this container directly; filesystem ownership or administrator access is not an absolute secrecy boundary. Expired or revoked server-side logins may need authentication again. The app manages the default local directories, not every custom Claude profile. The program-maintenance controls uninstall or reinstall Claude Code without removing the identity vault. ### Browser verification Open **Browser** or the companion browser's local test page to measure the actual environment. Checks cover the network exit, country, timezone, language, platform, CPU count, engine version and location settings. The success page appears only when the measured checks match, the report reaches the cleaner and no measurement error remains. **DNS and WebRTC leak checks are not independently verified.** A green result describes the measured checks, not a guarantee of anonymity or account acceptance. ### Network setup Open **Network** for three steps: **Get VPS → Get residential proxy → Install Skill**. Select **General**, **Codex**, **Cursor**, **OpenCode** or **Copilot**, then copy the installation prompt into your local coding agent. The prompt follows the app's English/Chinese setting. The [Network Skill](skills/ccbaga-network/README.md#installation) follows the Agent Skills specification and installs separately from the apps. It supports the npm `skills` CLI: `npx skills add liseami/CCBaga --skill ccbaga-network --global`; the AI selects the target tool, uses copy mode on Windows, and disables installer tracking. Give the AI your VPS address, the three matching PEM/PPK/PUB files or downloaded key bundle, and your residential SOCKS5 connection details. It handles file paths, private configuration, commands and checks; you do not need to open a terminal or edit JSON. Missing resources are purchased by you with the AI's guidance. Remote setup runs only after approval of the actual server changes. The Skill supports authorized Debian 12/13 servers using root key login on port 22. It checks the SSH identity and fixed SOCKS5 exit, configures Xray/Reality and delivers a private local import file after server self-checks pass. Client setup uses **TUN ON**, **System Proxy OFF** and an empty explicit browser proxy; actual TUN/browser verification remains a separate step. The subscription URL uses HTTP and contains credentials; prefer the file retrieved over SSH. Provider buttons link to [DMIT](https://www.dmit.io/aff.php?aff=28800) and [Webshare](https://www.webshare.io/?referral_code=qlm1mt9xibc9). Network setup is optional; local cleanup does not require a VPS or a proxy subscription. **The app does not collect SSH keys or proxy credentials and does not deploy to servers.** ## Architecture ![Pixel architecture map: native core, companion browser and a separate AI Network Skill](docs/architecture.svg) The UI owns inputs and presentation. Rust owns validation, task locks, process identity checks and execution. Small Objective-C bridges call macOS APIs; Rust Linux and Windows boundaries use native process identity checks and platform controls. The browser test page has no Tauri command access; it exchanges context and measurements through a random-token loopback session. | Layer | Technology | Responsibility | | --- | --- | --- | | Desktop host | Rust · Tauri 2 | Native commands, transactions, progress and lifecycle | | Interface | React 19 · TypeScript · Cromma UI | Forms, previews and execution results | | Platform bridges | AppKit · Security · CoreLocation · Linux / Windows Rust | Platform permissions and system integration | | Companion browser | Fingerprint Chromium | Dedicated profile and real browser measurements | | Separate Network Skill | Python standard library · OpenSSH · Bash · Xray | AI-managed private configuration, approved remote setup and server/client verification | | Localization | YAML · Vite | Build-time English/Chinese catalogs |
Repository map ```text assets/ Compressed brand logos and pixel-art DMG background src/ Desktop UI, browser test page and localization src-tauri/src/ Rust commands and transaction boundaries src-tauri/native/ Small macOS API bridges browser-runtime/ Engine metadata, launcher, entitlements and licenses scripts/ Icons, local builds and installation helpers skills/ Installable AI Network Skill and its execution scripts packaging/arch/ Native Arch Linux PKGBUILD and desktop entry docs/ README artwork and platform development guides vendor/cromma-ui/ Vendored interface components ``` The large browser application and archive are generated/runtime inputs, excluded from Git. `CLAUDE.md` files map module boundaries; source headers describe inputs, outputs and responsibilities.
## Development ### Prerequisites On Linux, follow [Linux setup](docs/linux.md). On macOS, use an Apple Silicon Mac with Xcode Command Line Tools, stable Rust and Bun. Follow [Tauri's macOS prerequisites](https://v2.tauri.app/start/prerequisites/#macos) for the native toolchain. The browser engine is an external build input. `python3 scripts/fetch-browser.py` downloads the pinned macOS arm64 **Fingerprint Chromium 148.0.7778.215** engine from the [upstream project](https://github.com/adryfish/fingerprint-chromium), verifies its SHA-256 and preserves its bundle structure and notices. Browser runtime binaries are not included in the source repository. From your checkout: ```sh bun install --frozen-lockfile python3 scripts/fetch-browser.py sh scripts/make-icons.sh sh scripts/package-browser.sh bun run tauri dev ``` Local builds are for development and testing; they are not official project downloads. ### Fast local build and install (macOS) ```sh bun run dev:install ``` This builds a debug app with the embedded UI, uses local ad-hoc signatures and installs/starts both apps. It does not use Apple credentials or create an installer. It preserves profiles and settings. The development installer accepts only locally built debug apps; downloaded installers still require the normal signature and Gatekeeper checks. ### Build ```sh MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=12.0 \ bun run tauri build --bundles app --features custom-protocol ``` The host bundle is written to `src-tauri/target/release/bundle/macos/CCBaga-A.app`. The companion bundle remains at `browser-runtime/Browser.app` until copied to Applications as `CCBaga-B.app`. Production builds require `custom-protocol` to load the embedded UI. Compilation without it fails explicitly, preventing an installed app from depending on the development server. ### Checks ```sh bun run build bun test MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=12.0 \ cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml python3 scripts/test-sign-browser.py python3 skills/ccbaga-network/scripts/test_network.py bash -n skills/ccbaga-network/scripts/setup-vps.sh ``` Pull requests run the existing frontend, native Rust, offline Skill and npm skill-installation checks on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows, plus the relevant platform regression tests. The workflow uses a read-only token, no signing secrets and no artifact uploads; it does not publish releases or download the browser engine. Complete engine and installer validation remains part of the separate delivery checks. The identity UI simulation uses 40 fictitious accounts, mocked Tauri IPC and an isolated headless context with external requests blocked. It covers card navigation, retention choices, switching, irreversible-delete alerts, failure recovery and both languages. Run `bun run test:identities` with Node.js 22.23.2 or later after preparing the pinned browser engine. The browser receives a temporary HOME/XDG configuration. Native archive tests use temporary SQLite databases and files; the macOS credential bridge is also checked against a separate disposable Keychain. Automated tests exercise disposable fixtures and local test servers. They do not deploy a real VPS, delete your Claude account data or perform administrator-authorized system changes. Real SSH connectivity, client-side TUN routing and permission-dependent operations require validation in the target environment. ## Data & permissions - **Identities are local.** Login state is archived before switching. You choose which personal data stays in the workspace and which is stored with the identity. Actual project source and cloud-side account records are outside this scope. - **Secrets stay out of UI logs.** The apps have no SSH key picker or server deployment command. After explicit confirmation, the native identity vault reads only the recognized default Claude credentials needed for restoration; credential contents never enter the GUI, command-line arguments or network. The separate Skill uses private local files and temporary private PEM copies (0600 on POSIX, verified user-only NTFS ACLs on Windows); data supplied to your coding agent is subject to that agent provider’s handling. - **Network checks make real requests.** Exit detection uses `ipwho.is` with `ipapi.co` as a fallback on the same route. IP location is a service estimate. - **Remote changes are explicit.** The separate Skill contacts only the VPS you provide after server-change approval. Required credentials remain in private local/server configuration, outside Git and public logs. - **Permissions are feature-specific.** Timezone changes require macOS administrator authorization. Keychain access follows system prompts. Location controls may require Accessibility permission or a manual action in System Settings. Custom `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` locations are not automatically included in the default identity scope. The app reports this limitation rather than silently claiming they were switched. ## Contributing Start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Small, focused changes with clear behavior and relevant checks are welcome. For bug reports, include the operating system and version, app version, operation and sanitized error; never attach private keys, passwords or subscription URLs. ## License & credits CCBaga's original project code is released under the **[MIT License](LICENSE)**. Third-party code and binaries retain their own terms; see [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md). Built with [Tauri](https://tauri.app/), [React](https://react.dev/) and [Fingerprint Chromium](https://github.com/adryfish/fingerprint-chromium), with a native macOS implementation of Claude maintenance workflows. Cleanup discovery was informed by the [claude-cleanup skill](https://github.com/suyuan2022/suyuan-skill/tree/main/claude-cleanup).
An independent project. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic or Apple.

repos.readme_excerpt:
ArtCraft Launcher

One place to install, update and open every app in the Craft App Suite, rebuilt in pure Rust.
PhotoCraft, LightCraft, FilmCraft, DesignCraft, VectorCraft, PdfCraft, EffectCraft, WordCraft,
DeckCraft, GridCraft, CADCraft, SoundCraft and FigCraft: the right build for your computer, kept up to date.

Download ArtCraft Launcher · ArtCraft · The Craft App Suite

> [!NOTE] > **ArtCraft is a community of artists from all walks of life.** Painters, photographers, > filmmakers, illustrators, designers, animators, hobbyists, and people who picked up a pencil > last week. If you make things, you're one of us. **[Come say hi on Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft).**

What it does · Features · Downloads · Build from source · Craft App Suite · Discord


Switch between the grid and a sortable table.

## What it does The Craft apps each ship their own builds for every platform. ArtCraft Launcher saves you from hunting through a dozen release pages: it lists every app in the suite, shows which ones you have and which version, installs the right build for your operating system and processor, and tells you when an update is out. It is a small native app that can sit in your menu bar or system tray. ## Features

📦 Install in one click

Picks the right download for your OS and CPU (DMG, MSI, AppImage, .deb, .rpm and more), checks it against the release's SHA-256 checksums and installs it.

🔄 Stay up to date

Checks each app's GitHub releases and updates the ones you have. A notification tells you when there's something new.

🧭 Always at hand

Opens any Craft app from one window, or from the tray and menu-bar icon. Native egui, no Electron, no web view.
The web version shows the same catalog in the browser, with the latest download for each app. ## Interface languages The interface is in English, Brazilian Portuguese (Português (Brasil)), Czech (Čeština), French (Français), German (Deutsch), Hungarian (Magyar), Japanese (日本語), Polish (Polski), Russian (Русский), Simplified Chinese (简体中文) or Spanish (Español). **Auto**, the default, follows the system or browser language; **Settings → Language** picks one and switches at once, and the choice is kept between runs. Czech locales (`cs-CZ`, `cs_CZ.UTF-8`…) select Czech, German ones (`de-DE`, `de-AT`, `de-CH`, `de_DE.UTF-8`…) German, French ones (`fr-FR`, `fr-CA`…) French, Hungarian ones (`hu`, `hu-HU`, `hu_HU.UTF-8`…) Hungarian, Japanese ones (`ja`, `ja-JP`, `ja_JP.UTF-8`…) Japanese, Polish ones (`pl`, `pl-PL`, `pl_PL.UTF-8`) Polish, Spanish ones (`es-ES`, `es-MX`, `es-419`…) Spanish, and Portuguese ones (`pt-BR`, and `pt-PT` too, for now) Brazilian Portuguese. Simplified Chinese locales (`zh-CN`, `zh-SG`, `zh-Hans`, and POSIX forms such as `zh_CN.UTF-8`) select Chinese; Traditional Chinese ones don't. To try a language without changing the setting, start the desktop app with `ARTCRAFT_LAUNCHER_LOCALE=pt-BR`, or add `?lang=ru` to the web address. The CJK languages are drawn with the system's own CJK font (Hiragino Sans or PingFang on macOS, Yu Gothic, Meiryo or Microsoft YaHei on Windows, Noto Sans CJK, IPA, Takao or WenQuanYi on Linux and FreeBSD). Where the system has no font for one, and in the web version, the interface stays in English and Settings says why. Product names and release notes stay as published; text without a translation falls back to English. ## Where apps are installed ArtCraft Launcher installs each app where your system normally keeps applications, using the app's official release package, so an app installed by the launcher is the same as one you installed by hand (and the launcher finds apps you installed yourself): | System | Where | How | |---|---|---| | macOS | `/Applications/.app` | Copied from the signed, notarized release DMG | | Windows | `C:\Program Files\` | The release MSI, through Windows Installer (with Start menu entry and Apps & features entry) | | Linux | `/usr/bin`, `/usr/share/applications` | The release `.deb` (apt) or `.rpm` (dnf, zypper), with your system's password prompt. Without those, a Flatpak, or an AppImage in `~/Applications` | | Linux, inside the launcher's Flatpak, with no Flatpak on the host | `~/.var/app/ai.storyteller.artcraft-launcher/data/artcraft-launcher/apps/` | The release tarball, unpacked into the launcher's own folder and run inside the same sandbox, with its settings in a `home/` folder beside it. Nothing is installed on the host, and each app's configuration stays in the sandbox | | FreeBSD | `/usr/local` | The release tree, with a password prompt (polkit); `~/.local` when polkit isn't installed | ArtCraft Launcher keeps itself current too: when a new version is out, **Update and restart** downloads it, verifies it, puts it where this copy is installed (the `.app`, the Windows Installer package or portable folder, the AppImage, or the `.deb`/`.rpm`) and reopens it. Updates use the same format an app was installed with. Every download is checked against the release's published SHA-256 before it is installed, and a running app is never replaced. The launcher writes its log to `logs/artcraft-launcher.log` in its data folder (`~/.local/share/artcraft-launcher` on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/ArtCraft Launcher` on macOS, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ArtCraft Launcher` on Windows, `ArtCraftLauncherData` beside the portable zip's executable) and keeps the previous two runs as `artcraft-launcher.1.log` and `artcraft-launcher.2.log`. `RUST_LOG` changes what it records (`debug`, `info,zbus=warn`, …). ## Downloads Download the build for your computer from the [latest release](https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/releases/latest), or browse [all releases](https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/releases). Every release has a `SHA256SUMS.txt` to check the files against. `` is the version number, for example `0.1.0`. **Windows** (10 and 11) | File | What it is | |---|---| | `artcraft-launcher--windows-x64.msi` | Installer for most PCs (Intel and AMD, 64-bit). Installs for the current user, no admin rights needed | | `artcraft-launcher--windows-arm64.msi` | Installer for Windows on Arm (Snapdragon and other Arm PCs) | | `artcraft-launcher--windows-x86.msi` | Installer for 32-bit Windows | | `artcraft-launcher--windows-{x64,arm64,x86}-portable.zip` | No install: unzip and run `artcraft-launcher.exe`. Keeps its settings in the folder | **macOS** (11 Big Sur or later) | File | What it is | |---|---| | `artcraft-launcher--macos-universal.dmg` | Universal app for Apple silicon and Intel Macs, signed and notarized. Drag ArtCraft Launcher to Applications | **Linux** (x86_64 and aarch64; glibc 2.35 or newer, e.g. Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, Fedora 36+) | File | What it is | |---|---| | `artcraft-launcher--linux-{x86_64,aarch64}.AppImage` | Runs on almost any distro without installing; `chmod +x` and run. The `.AppImage.zsync` beside it lets AppImageUpdate fetch only what changed | | `artcraft-launcher--linux-{x86_64,aarch64}.deb` | Debian, Ubuntu, Mint, Pop!_OS: `sudo apt install ./artcraft-launcher-…deb` | | `artcraft-launcher--linux-{x86_64,aarch64}.rpm` | Fedora, openSUSE, RHEL: `sudo dnf install ./artcraft-launcher-…rpm` | | `artcraft-launcher--linux-{x86_64,aarch64}.flatpak` | Flatpak bundle: `flatpak install --user artcraft-launcher-…flatpak`. Inside the sandbox the launcher installs apps as Flatpaks on the host through `flatpak-spawn --host`; where the host has no Flatpak it falls back to each app's release tarball, unpacked and run inside the sandbox with the app's settings kept in it. Either way it can only reach the host as far as that permission allows; the AppImage, .deb and .rpm builds are the recommended way to run the launcher on Linux | | `artcraft-launcher--linux-{x86_64,aarch64}.tar.gz` | Plain tree (`bin/`, `share/`) for everyone else and for scripts | RISC-V (riscv64): `artcraft-launcher--linux-riscv64.{deb,rpm,tar.gz}`, built against Ubuntu 24.04 (needs glibc 2.39+). The tray icon uses the StatusNotifierItem standard: KDE, Xfce, Cinnamon and most other desktops show it; on GNOME install the AppIndicator extension. **FreeBSD** (14, x86_64) | File | What it is | |---|---| | `artcraft-launcher--freebsd-x86_64.tar.gz` | A tree laid out like `/usr/local` | ```sh pkg install libxkbcommon wayland libX11 libXcursor libXrandr libXi libxcb mesa-libs vulkan-loader fontconfig freetype2 tar -xzf artcraft-launcher--freebsd-x86_64.tar.gz --strip-components 1 -C /usr/local artcraft-launcher ``` **Web (WebAssembly)** | File | What it is | |---|---| | `artcraft-launcher-web-.zip` | The catalog as a static site you can host anywhere; see [`packaging/web/README.md`](packaging/web/README.md) | ## Build from source You need a recent stable Rust (1.90 or newer). On Linux, install the windowing headers first (Debian/Ubuntu: `sudo apt install libxkbcommon-dev libwayland-dev libx11-dev libxrandr-dev libxi-dev libgl1-mesa-dev`). ```sh git clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher cd craft-launcher cargo run --release -p artcraft-launcher # the desktop app cargo xtask ci # fmt, clippy, tests and the wasm check ``` The web version builds with [trunk](https://trunkrs.dev/): ```sh rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown cd apps/artcraft-launcher-web && trunk serve ``` ### Installing your own builds To install and update the Craft apps from checkouts on your machine instead of GitHub, clone them next to this repo (`../photocraft`, `../wordcraft`, …) and run: ```sh cargo xtask local sync # git pull every app, build and package each new version into ../local-mirror cargo xtask local serve # serve the builds and a release feed on http://127.0.0.1:8787/ ARTCRAFT_LAUNCHER_DOWNLOAD_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:8787/ cargo run --release -p artcraft-launcher --features local-mirror ``` Run `sync` again whenever you want updates, or let the server do it: `cargo xtask local serve --sync-every 1h` pulls and builds on that interval while it serves. An app is rebuilt when its checkout's version isn't in the mirror yet (`--rebuild` forces it), and the launcher's next check picks it up. Add `--every-commit` to build every new commit instead, as a dev version between releases (`0.4.0` builds as `0.4.1-dev.`), which the launcher offers as an update. While `ARTCRAFT_LAUNCHER_DOWNLOAD_BASE` is set (loopback addresses only), the launcher asks only the mirror, never GitHub. Only builds with the `local-mirror` feature read it; releases never have it. `cargo xtask local help` lists the options (`--only`, `--no-pull`, `--arch`, …). New contributors and AI agents: start with [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md). Release packaging lives in [`packaging/`](packaging/) and [`.github/workflows/release.yml`](.github/workflows/release.yml). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Status:** ArtCraft Launcher is new and in early alpha. Expect rough edges, and please file > issues (include your OS, which app you were installing and the launcher's log file) or tell us on > [Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft). ## The Craft App Suite ArtCraft Launcher installs the **Craft App Suite**: free, open-source creative tools from the [ArtCraft](https://getartcraft.com/) team, each written from scratch in Rust and each able to stand on its own. | | App | What it's for | Code | Learn more | |:-:|---|---|---|---| | | **PhotoCraft** | Image editing: layers, masks, type and real PSD files | [GitHub](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft) want real control.

Come make things with us

Our Discord is where artists of every kind hang out: people who paint, shoot, draw, cut film, set type, and people still figuring out what they like to make.
